title: Switch activity shortcut order
line: Holding Meta and pressing A repeatedly now walks through activities in most-recently-used order, like Alt+Tab, instead of bouncing back after the first step.
explanation: The activity switcher froze its most-recently-used list (setInhibitUpdates) only when it decided to show itself, 100 ms after Meta+A. The first switch therefore happened with a live list: the new activity jumped to the top and its last-used time was saved, so the next Meta+A went back to where you started and later single switches went to the wrong activity. Now the list is frozen as soon as Meta+A is pressed, and the order and last-used times are committed only once the modifier is released (or right away for a single tap).

commits.message:
activitymanager: freeze the activity order on the first Meta+A press

The switcher only froze the most-recently-used order once it decided to
show itself, so the first switch already reordered the list and saved
its time, sending later presses back. Freeze it on the keypress instead.

BUG: 419499

media.caption: MRU order C, B, A. Holding Meta: first A goes to B, which jumps to the top; second A goes back to C.
Same steps: the list stays C, B, A and the second A reaches A.
Walk C→B→C, then a single Meta+A goes to B instead of the previous activity.
Walk C→B→A, then a single Meta+A returns to C.

review.text: Fixes the root cause: the MRU list was only frozen once the switcher decided to show (100 ms later), so the first switch reordered it and saved its time. Freezing it on the key press and committing on release (or immediately for a single tap via setShouldShowSwitcher(false)) is minimal and matches what jpetso's stale !1546 aimed for. One edge to double-check: showActivitySwitcherIfNeeded() returns early when m_dropModeActive, which would leave inhibitUpdates stuck true until the next Meta+A. Clearing it there would make it robust.
